verses.1:1: The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.1:2: And he said: "The Lord will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem He will give His voice; and the beautiful places of the shepherds have mourned, and the summit of Carmel has dried up."
verses.1:3: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with iron wagons.
verses.1:4: And I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the houses of Ben-hadad.
verses.1:5: And I will break the bar of Damascus, and I will destroy the inhabitant from the plain of the idol, and the one holding the scepter from the house of pleasure; and the people of Syria will be carried away to Cyrene," says the Lord.
verses.1:6: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried away a complete captivity, to shut it up in Idumea.
verses.1:7: And I will send fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its dwellings.
verses.1:8: And I will destroy the inhabitant from Ashdod, and the one holding the scepter from Ashkelon; and I will turn My hand against Ekron, and the rest of the Philistines will perish," says the Lord God.
verses.1:9: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they shut up a complete captivity in Idumea, and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
verses.1:10: And I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its dwellings."
verses.1:11: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword, and violated his mercy, and held his fury further, and kept his indignation until the end.
verses.1:12: I will send fire into Teman, and it will devour the dwellings of Bozrah."
verses.1:13: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he cut open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge his border.
verses.1:14: And I will kindle a fire on the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its dwellings with wailing in the day of war, and with a whirlwind in the day of upheaval.
verses.1:15: And Milcom will go into captivity, he and his princes together," says the Lord.
verses.2:1: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because it burned the bones of the king of Idumea to ashes.
verses.2:2: And I will send fire into Moab, and it will devour the dwellings of Kerioth; and Moab will die with uproar, with the blare of the trumpet.
verses.2:3: And I will destroy the judge from its midst, and I will kill all its princes with him," says the Lord.
verses.2:4: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because it rejected the law of the Lord and did not keep His commandments; for their idols had deceived them, after which their fathers had gone.
verses.2:5: And I will send fire into Judah, and it will devour the dwellings of Jerusalem."
verses.2:6: The Lord says this: "For three crimes of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because it sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for sandals.
verses.2:7: They crush the heads of the poor upon the dust of the earth, and turn aside the way of the humble; and a son and his father went to the girl, to violate My holy name.
verses.2:8: And upon pledged garments they reclined beside every altar, and they were drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their God.
verses.2:9: Yet I wiped out the Amorite from before their face, whose height was the height of cedars, and he himself was strong like an oak; and I crushed his fruit from above, and his roots beneath.
verses.2:10: It is I who made you come up from the land of Egypt, and led you in the desert for forty years, so that you might possess the land of the Amorite.
verses.2:11: And I raised up prophets from your sons, and Nazirites from your young men. Is it not so, sons of Israel?" says the Lord.
verses.2:12: "And you will give the Nazirites wine to drink, and you will command the prophets, saying, 'Do not prophesy.'
verses.2:13: Look, I will creak beneath you, just as a wagon loaded with hay creaks.
verses.2:14: And flight will perish from the swift, and the strong will not retain his strength, and the mighty will not save his life;
verses.2:15: and the one holding the bow will not stand, and the one swift on his feet will not be saved, and the rider of a horse will not save his life;
verses.2:16: and the mighty in heart among the strong will flee naked in that day," says the Lord.
verses.3:1: Hear the word that the Lord has spoken against you, sons of Israel, against the whole family that I brought out from the land of Egypt, saying:
verses.3:2: "You alone have I known out of all the families of the earth; therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities."
verses.3:3: Will two walk together, unless they have agreed?
verses.3:4: Will a lion roar in the forest, unless it has prey? Will a lion cub give voice from its den, unless it has caught something?
verses.3:5: Will a bird fall into a snare on the ground without a bird-catcher? Will a snare be taken away from the ground before it has caught anything?
verses.3:6: Will a trumpet blare in a city, and the people not be terrified? Will there be evil in a city that the Lord has not done?
verses.3:7: For the Lord God does not do a thing, unless He has revealed His secret to His servants the prophets.
verses.3:8: A lion will roar; who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken; who will not prophesy?
verses.3:9: Make it heard in the dwellings of Ashdod, and in the dwellings of the land of Egypt, and say: "Assemble upon the mountains of Samaria, and see the many acts of madness in its midst, and those suffering oppression in its inner chambers."
verses.3:10: "And they did not know how to do what is right," says the Lord, "storing up iniquity and plunder in their dwellings."
verses.3:11: Therefore the Lord God says this: "The land will be afflicted and surrounded, and your strength will be stripped from you, and your dwellings will be plundered."
verses.3:12: The Lord says this: "Just as if a shepherd rescues from the mouth of a lion two legs, or the tip of an ear, so will the sons of Israel be rescued, who dwell in Samaria on the corner of a couch, and on a bed of Damascus."
verses.3:13: "Hear, and bear witness in the house of Jacob," says the Lord God of hosts;
verses.3:14: "for in the day when I begin to visit the transgressions of Israel, I will visit upon him, and upon the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar will be cut off, and they will fall to the ground.
verses.3:15: And I will strike the winter house with the summer house, and the ivory houses will perish, and many dwellings will be demolished," says the Lord.
verses.4:1: Hear this word, fat cows who are on the mountain of Samaria, who defraud the needy and crush the poor, who say to your masters, "Bring it, and we will drink."
verses.4:2: The Lord God has sworn by His holiness, "Look, days will come upon you, and they will lift you up on poles, and your remnants in boiling pots.
verses.4:3: And you will go out through the openings, one opposite another, and you will be cast into Armon," says the Lord.
verses.4:4: "Come to Bethel and act wickedly; to Gilgal, and multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes every three days.
verses.4:5: And sacrifice a praise offering from what is leavened, and proclaim freewill offerings, and announce them; for so you have desired, sons of Israel," says the Lord God.
verses.4:6: "Therefore I also gave you numbness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet you did not return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:7: "I also withheld the rain from you when three months still remained until the harvest; and I sent rain upon one city, and upon another city I did not send rain; one part was rained upon, and the part upon which I did not send rain dried up.
verses.4:8: And two and three cities came to one city to drink water, and they were not satisfied; yet you did not return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:9: "I struck you with a scorching wind and with mildew; the caterpillar devoured the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards, your olive groves and your fig orchards; yet you did not return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:10: "I sent death among you in the way of Egypt; I struck your young men with the sword, even to the capture of your horses, and I caused the stench of your camps to rise into your nostrils; yet you did not return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:11: "I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched from the blaze; yet you did not return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:12: "Therefore I will do these things to you, Israel; and after I have done these things to you, prepare yourself to meet your God, Israel."
verses.4:13: For look, He who forms the mountains, and creates the wind, and announces His speech to man, making the morning mist, and treading upon the heights of the earth: the Lord God of hosts is His name.
verses.5:1: Hear this word which I lift up over you as a lamentation: The house of Israel has fallen, and will not rise again.
verses.5:2: The virgin Israel has been cast down onto her own land; there is no one to raise her up.
verses.5:3: For this is what the Lord God says: "The city from which a thousand went out will have a hundred left in it, and the one from which a hundred went out will have ten left in it, in the house of Israel."
verses.5:4: For this is what the Lord says to the house of Israel: "Seek Me, and you will live.
verses.5:5: And do not seek Bethel, and do not enter Gilgal, and you will not cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal will be led captive, and Bethel will be useless."
verses.5:6: Seek the Lord and live (otherwise the house of Joseph may be burned like fire, and it will devour, and there will be no one to quench Bethel,
verses.5:7: you who turn judgment into wormwood and leave righteousness on the ground),
verses.5:8: Him who makes Arcturus and Orion, and turns darkness into morning, and changes day into night; who calls the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth; the Lord is His name;
verses.5:9: who smiles destruction upon the strong and brings devastation upon the mighty.
verses.5:10: They have hated the one who rebukes in the gate, and they have detested the one who speaks perfectly.
verses.5:11: Therefore, because you were plundering the poor man and taking choice plunder from him, you will build houses of squared stone, and you will not live in them; you will plant most lovely vineyards, and you will not drink their wine.
verses.5:12: For I know your many crimes and your mighty sins: enemies of the righteous one, taking a bribe, and pressing down the poor in the gate.
verses.5:13: Therefore the prudent one will keep silent in that time, for the time is evil.
verses.5:14: Seek good and not evil, so that you may live; and the Lord God of hosts will be with you, just as you have said.
verses.5:15: Hate evil and love good, and establish judgment in the gate; perhaps the Lord God of hosts will have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.
verses.5:16: Therefore this is what the Lord God of hosts, the Ruler, says: "In all the public squares there will be lamentation, and in all places that are outside it will be said, 'Woe, woe!' And they will call the farmer to mourning, and to lamentation those who know how to lament.
verses.5:17: And in all the vineyards there will be lamentation, for I will pass through your midst," says the Lord.
verses.5:18: Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord! For what purpose is it to you? This day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.
verses.5:19: Just as if a man flees from the face of a lion, and a bear meets him; and he enters a house, and leans with his hand upon the wall, and a snake bites him.
verses.5:20: Is not the day of the Lord darkness, and not light, and gloom, and no brightness in it?
verses.5:21: "I hate and have cast aside your festivals, and I will not take in the aroma of your assemblies.
verses.5:22: And if you offer Me burnt offerings and your gifts, I will not accept them; and I will not look upon the vowed offerings of your fattened animals.
verses.5:23: Take away from Me the uproar of your songs, and I will not listen to the melodies of your lyre.
verses.5:24: And judgment will be revealed like water, and righteousness like a mighty torrent.
verses.5:25: Did you present to Me sacrifices and an offering in the desert for forty years, house of Israel?
verses.5:26: And you carried the tabernacle for your Moloch, and the image of your idols, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves.
verses.5:27: And I will cause you to go into exile beyond Damascus," says the Lord; God of hosts is His name.
verses.6:1: Woe to you who are wealthy in Zion and trust in the mountain of Samaria, you nobles, heads of the peoples, entering the house of Israel with pomp!
verses.6:2: Cross over to Calneh and see, and go from there to great Hamath, and go down to Gath of the Philistines, and to all the finest of these kingdoms: whether their border is wider than your border.
verses.6:3: You who are set apart for the evil day, and draw near to the throne of iniquity;
verses.6:4: who sleep on ivory beds and act wantonly on your couches; who eat a lamb from the flock and calves from the midst of the herd;
verses.6:5: who sing to the sound of the harp; like David they thought they had instruments of song,
verses.6:6: drinking wine in bowls and anointed with the finest ointment, yet they suffered nothing over the crushing of Joseph.
verses.6:7: Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of those going into exile, and the faction of those who act wantonly will be taken away.
verses.6:8: The Lord God has sworn by His soul, says the Lord God of hosts: "I detest the pride of Jacob, and I hate his houses, and I will hand over the city with its inhabitants."
verses.6:9: And if ten men are left in one house, they also will die.
verses.6:10: And his relative will take him up and burn him, to carry the bones out of the house; and he will say to the one who is in the innermost parts of the house, "Is there still anyone with you?"
verses.6:11: For look, the Lord will command, and will strike the larger house with ruins, and the smaller house with cracks.
verses.6:12: Can horses run on rocks, or can one plow with wild oxen? For you have turned judgment into bitterness, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
verses.6:13: You who rejoice in nothing, who say, "Have we not by our own strength taken horns for ourselves?"
verses.6:14: "For look, I will raise up against you, house of Israel," says the Lord God of hosts, "a nation, and it will crush you from the entrance of Hamath to the torrent of the desert."
verses.7:1: The Lord God showed me these things: and look, a maker of the locust at the beginning of the sprouting shoots of the late rain, and look, the late rain after the king's shearing.
verses.7:2: And it happened, when it had finished eating the grass of the land, I said, "Lord God, be merciful, I plead; who will raise up Jacob, for he is very small?"
verses.7:3: The Lord had compassion over this: "It will not be," said the Lord.
verses.7:4: The Lord God showed me these things: and look, the Lord God was calling judgment to fire; and it devoured the vast abyss, and ate the portion at the same time.
verses.7:5: And I said, "Lord God, cease, I plead; who will raise up Jacob, for he is very small?"
verses.7:6: The Lord had compassion over this: "Even this will not be," said the Lord God.
verses.7:7: The Lord showed me these things: and look, the Lord standing upon a plastered wall, and in His hand a mason's trowel.
verses.7:8: And the Lord said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A mason's trowel." And the Lord said, "Look, I will place a trowel in the midst of My people Israel; I will no longer plaster over them.
verses.7:9: And the high places of the idol will be demolished, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be made desolate, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
verses.7:10: And Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying, "Amos has rebelled against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land will not be able to bear all his words.
verses.7:11: For Amos says these things: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will go away captive from its land.'"
verses.7:12: And Amaziah said to Amos, "You who see, go: flee into the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and you will prophesy there.
verses.7:13: And in Bethel you will no longer prophesy, for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is the house of the kingdom."
verses.7:14: And Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I am not a prophet, and I am not a son of a prophet, but I am a herdsman, plucking sycamores.
verses.7:15: And the Lord took me while I was following the flock, and the Lord said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'
verses.7:16: And now hear the word of the Lord: you say, 'You will not prophesy against Israel, and you will not drip upon the house of the idol.'
verses.7:17: Because of this, the Lord says these things: 'Your wife will act as a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword, and your ground will be measured with a line; and you will die in a polluted land, and Israel will go away captive from its land.'"
verses.8:1: The Lord God showed me these things: and look, a hook for fruit.
verses.8:2: And He said, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A hook for fruit." And the Lord said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will no longer pass by them."
verses.8:3: "And the hinges of the temple will creak in that day," says the Lord God: "Many will die; in every place silence will be cast."
verses.8:4: Hear this, you who crush the poor, and cause the needy of the land to fail,
verses.8:5: saying, "When will the month pass, and we will sell merchandise? And the Sabbath, and we will open the grain, so that we may diminish the measure, and increase the shekel, and substitute deceitful scales,
verses.8:6: so that we may possess the needy for silver and the poor for sandals, and sell the refuse of the grain?"
verses.8:7: The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob: "Surely I will not forget all their works to the end."
verses.8:8: Will the land not tremble over this, and every inhabitant of it mourn, and all of it rise like a river, and be cast out, and flow down like the stream of Egypt?
verses.8:9: "And it will be in that day," says the Lord God, "the sun will set at noon, and I will make the earth grow dark on a day of light;
verses.8:10: and I will turn your festivals into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation, and I will bring sackcloth upon every back of yours, and baldness upon every head; and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day."
verses.8:11: "Look, days are coming," the Lord will say, "and I will send a famine into the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the word of the Lord."
verses.8:12: And they will stagger from sea to sea, and from the north to the east; they will go around seeking the word of the Lord, and will not find it.
verses.8:13: In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst,
verses.8:14: who swear by the offense of Samaria, and say, "Your god lives, Dan, and the way of Beersheba lives"; and they will fall, and will not rise up again.
verses.9:1: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and He said, "Strike the hinge, and let the lintels shake: for greed is on the head of all, and the last of them I will kill with the sword; there will be no flight for them. They will flee, and the one who flees from among them will not be saved.
verses.9:2: If they descend all the way to hell, from there My hand will bring them out; and if they ascend all the way to heaven, from there I will pull them down.
verses.9:3: And if they are hidden on the summit of Carmel, from there, searching, I will take them away; and if they conceal themselves from My eyes in the depth of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
verses.9:4: And if they go away into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it will kill them; and I will set My eyes upon them for evil, and not for good."
verses.9:5: And the Lord God of hosts, who touches the earth, and it will melt, and all who dwell in it will mourn; and all of it will rise like a stream, and flow down like the river of Egypt.
verses.9:6: He who builds His ascent in heaven, and has founded His bundle upon the earth; who calls the waters of the sea, and pours them out upon the face of the earth: the Lord is His name.
verses.9:7: "Are you not like the sons of the Ethiopians to Me, sons of Israel?" says the Lord. "Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Cappadocia, and the Syrians from Cyrene?"
verses.9:8: "Look, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinning kingdom, and I will crush it from the face of the earth; yet I will not completely crush the house of Jacob," says the Lord.
verses.9:9: "For look, I Myself will command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, just as wheat is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble will fall to the ground.
verses.9:10: All the sinners of My people will die by the sword, who say, 'Evil will not draw near, and will not come upon us.'"
verses.9:11: "In that day I will raise up the tent of David that has fallen, and I will rebuild the openings of its walls, and I will restore the things that had collapsed; and I will rebuild it as in ancient days,
verses.9:12: so that they may possess the remnant of Idumea and all the nations, because My name has been called upon them," says the Lord who does these things.
verses.9:13: "Look, days are coming," says the Lord, "and the plowman will overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes the one casting seed; and the mountains will drip sweetness, and all the hills will be cultivated.
verses.9:14: And I will turn back the captivity of My people Israel; and they will build deserted cities, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and drink their wine; and they will make gardens, and eat their fruits.
verses.9:15: And I will plant them upon their own ground, and I will no longer uproot them from their land, which I have given to them," says the Lord your God.

notes.1:2: Latin speciosa pastorum ("the beautiful places of the shepherds") translates Hebrew "pastures of the shepherds" via the root meaning "beautiful," and the Vulgate shifts to past-tense verbs (luxerunt, exsiccatus est) after the initial futures.
notes.1:3: Latin non convertam eum (literally "I will not turn him/it back") recurs across the oracles in 1:3-2:6 and may denote either not revoking the decreed punishment or not turning the offending nation back to repentance.
notes.1:5: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place names Biq'at-Aven and Beth-Eden literally as "the plain of the idol" (campo idoli) and "the house of pleasure" (domo voluptatis), and renders Hebrew Kir as Cyrenen (Cyrene).
notes.1:6: Here and in 1:9 and 2:1 the Vulgate uses the Greco-Roman territorial name Idumaea (Idumea) for Hebrew Edom, whereas 1:11 uses Edom.
notes.1:15: The Vulgate reads the proper name Melchom (Milcom, the national deity of the Ammonites), whereas the Masoretic vocalization reads "their king."
notes.2:1: Latin usque ad cinerem reads "to ashes," whereas the Hebrew text reads "to lime."
notes.2:4: Latin idola sua reads "their idols," a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew text reads "their lies."
notes.2:12: The Clementine Vulgate uses future-tense verbs (propinabitis, mandabitis, "you will give ... to drink," "you will command"), whereas the Hebrew text uses past-tense verbs.
notes.2:13: Latin stridebo subter vos, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum foeno ("I will creak beneath you, just as a wagon loaded with hay creaks") preserves a distinctively Vulgate wording where Hebrew refers to pressing down or groaning like a cart loaded with sheaves.
notes.3:2: Latin visitabo ("I will visit," also in 3:14) follows the biblical idiom of judicial inspection, meaning to call to account and punish.
notes.3:5: Latin absque aucupe ("without a bird-catcher") and auferetur laqueus ("will a snare be taken away") reflect Vulgate readings distinct from the Hebrew phrasing concerning a lure and a trap springing up.
notes.3:6: Latin malum ("evil") here refers to disaster or calamity sent in judgment rather than moral wickedness.
notes.3:11: Latin Tribulabitur et circuietur terra ("The land will be afflicted and surrounded") renders the Hebrew clause ("an adversary shall surround the land") as two passive verbs with "the land" as subject.
notes.3:12: Latin in Damasci grabato ("on a bed of Damascus") takes the difficult Hebrew phrase as naming Damascus rather than denoting silken cushions or part of a bed.
notes.4:1: The Vulgate translates Hebrew "cows of Bashan" as "fat cows" (vaccae pingues), interpreting the place name Bashan as denoting richness or fatness.
notes.4:2: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew fishing imagery ("with hooks ... with fishhooks") as "on poles" (in contis) and "in boiling pots" (in ollis ferventibus).
notes.4:3: The Vulgate preserves "Armon" (in Armon), corresponding to the obscure Hebrew term Harmon, whose location and meaning are uncertain.
notes.4:6: Where the Hebrew has "cleanness of teeth" (an idiom for famine), the Vulgate reads "numbness of teeth" (stuporem dentium).
notes.4:13: The Vulgate reads "announces His speech to man" (annuntians homini eloquium suum) and "making the morning mist" (faciens matutinam nebulam), where the Hebrew has "declares to man what his thought is" and "who makes dawn into darkness."
notes.5:1: Following the Clementine Vulgate verse division and punctuation, "the house of Israel" begins the lament as the subject of "has fallen," whereas the Hebrew joins "house of Israel" to the opening summons and places "has fallen" in verse 2.
notes.5:6: The Vulgate renders the warning passively with "the house of Joseph" as subject ("may be burned like fire," comburatur ut ignis) and places verses 6b-7 in parentheses so that the accusative participles of verse 8 ("Him who makes...") connect directly to "the Lord" in verse 6.
notes.5:8: The Vulgate names the constellation "Arcturus" (Arcturum) where the Hebrew reads "Pleiades."
notes.5:9: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew verb ("flashes") as "smiles" (subridet) and reads "the mighty" (potentem) where the Hebrew has "fortress."
notes.5:24: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew verb ("let roll down") as "will be revealed" (revelabitur), deriving it from the similar Hebrew root meaning "to uncover or reveal."
notes.5:26: The Vulgate reads "the tabernacle for your Moloch" (with dative Moloch vestro) and "the image of your idols," where the Hebrew names the deities "Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images."
notes.6:1: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "at ease" as "wealthy" (opulenti) and "to whom the house of Israel comes" as "entering the house of Israel with pomp" (ingredientes pompatice domum Israel).
notes.6:3: Where the Hebrew has "who put far away the evil day," the Vulgate uses a passive verb, "who are set apart for the evil day" (separati estis in diem malum).
notes.6:5: The Vulgate reads "they thought they had instruments of song" (putaverunt se habere vasa cantici) where the Hebrew has "they invent for themselves instruments of song."
notes.6:10: This Latin text ends verse 10 with the question "Is there still anyone with you?", without the further reply found in the Hebrew and in some Vulgate witnesses.
notes.6:12: The Vulgate specifies "wild oxen" (in bubalis) rather than ordinary oxen, and uses an impersonal passive ("can one plow," arari potest).
notes.7:1: Latin reads "maker of the locust" (fictor locustae) and "late rain" (serotini imbris ... serotinus), whereas the Hebrew refers to forming locusts as the late crop begins to sprout; tonsionem can mean either shearing flocks or mowing grass.
notes.7:2: Latin reads "who will raise up Jacob" (quis suscitabit Jacob, also in 7:5) and "had compassion" (misertus est, 7:3, 6), where the Hebrew has "how can Jacob stand?" and "relented."
notes.7:7: Latin reads "plastered wall" (murum litum) and "mason's trowel" (trulla caementarii), continuing the plastering image in 7:8 with "plaster over" (superinducere), where the Hebrew speaks of a plumb line and passing by or sparing.
notes.7:9: Latin reads "of the idol" (idoli, and "house of the idol" in 7:16), where the Hebrew has the name "Isaac."
notes.8:1: Latin reads "a hook for fruit" (uncinus pomorum, also in 8:2), whereas the Hebrew refers to a basket of summer fruit.
notes.8:3: Latin reads "the hinges of the temple will creak" (stridebunt cardines templi), where the Hebrew reads "the songs of the temple/palace will wail."
notes.8:7: "Surely I will not forget" renders the literal Latin conditional oath Si oblitus fuero ("If I have forgotten [may it not be]"), and "to the end" (usque ad finem) renders the Hebrew for "forever."
notes.8:11: The Clementine Vulgate reads the future tense dicet Dominus ("the Lord will say") rather than the present tense "says the Lord."
notes.9:1: Latin reads "hinge" (cardinem), "lintels" (superliminaria), and "for greed is on the head of all" (avaritia enim in capite omnium), where the Hebrew speaks of striking the capitals so the thresholds shake and shattering them on the head of all.
notes.9:6: Latin reads "His bundle" (fasciculum suum), rendering a Hebrew term often translated "His vault" or "His band."
notes.9:7: The Vulgate names "Cappadocia" and "Cyrene" where the Hebrew reads Caphtor and Kir, and renders Hebrew Cushites as "Ethiopians" (Aethiopum).
notes.9:12: Latin reads "the remnant of Idumea" (reliquias Idumaeae, corresponding to Hebrew Edom), whereas the Septuagint cited in Acts 15:17 reads "the remnant of mankind."
notes.9:13: Latin reads "will drip sweetness" (stillabunt ... dulcedinem) and "all the hills will be cultivated" (omnes colli culti erunt), where the Hebrew speaks of dripping sweet wine and all the hills melting or flowing.
